elements.element: Vendor must defend Customer against covered third-party claims.
elements.evidence: Article XIII-A requires Licensor to “defend” Licensee against any third-party claim arising from the enumerated events.

elements.element: Vendor must indemnify Customer against covered third-party claims and resulting losses.
elements.evidence: Article XIII-A requires Licensor to indemnify Licensee for third-party claims and all resulting damages, costs, expenses, and reasonable attorneys’ fees.

elements.element: Customer’s affiliates must be protected by Vendor’s defense and indemnity.
elements.evidence: Article XIII-A expressly covers Licensee “and its affiliates.”

elements.element: Vendor’s indemnity must cover third-party allegations that the services or deliverables infringe or misappropriate intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: Article XIII-A covers allegations that the Licensed Technology, services, or deliverables infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right.

elements.element: Vendor’s indemnity must cover third-party claims arising from Vendor’s breach of applicable law.
elements.evidence: Article XIII-A(ii) expressly covers “Licensor’s breach of applicable law.”

elements.element: Vendor’s indemnity must cover third-party claims arising from a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: Article XIII-A(iii) covers unauthorized access to or disclosure of Licensee’s data caused by Licensor.

elements.element: Vendor’s indemnity must cover third-party claims arising from Vendor’s gross negligence or wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: Article XIII-A(iv) expressly covers Licensor’s gross negligence or wilful misconduct.

elements.element: Customer must provide prompt notice of an indemnified claim.
elements.evidence: Article XIII-A requires Licensee to give Licensor prompt written notice.

elements.element: Vendor must control the defense of an indemnified claim.
elements.evidence: Article XIII-A states that Licensor shall have control of the defense.

elements.element: Customer must provide reasonable cooperation in the defense.
elements.evidence: Article XIII-A requires Licensee to provide reasonable cooperation.

elements.element: Customer’s indemnity must cover Customer-provided content.
elements.evidence: Revised Article XII limits item (i) to “content provided by Licensee.”

elements.element: Customer’s indemnity must cover Customer’s breach of applicable law.
elements.evidence: Article XII does not clearly state a Licensee breach-of-law trigger. It instead refers to “the breach by the License” of representations, warranties, obligations, restrictions, terms, or covenants “under applicable law,” using the wrong party designation and potentially contractual concepts.

elements.element: Customer’s indemnity must be limited exclusively to Customer-provided content and Customer’s breach of applicable law.
elements.evidence: The malformed second trigger potentially extends beyond breach of law, and Article XII also retains the broad statement that Licensee is solely responsible for any liability arising from its exercise of license rights.

elements.element: Vendor must provide an intellectual-property indemnity for third-party infringement claims concerning the services or deliverables.
elements.evidence: Article XIII-A provides a defense and indemnity for third-party claims alleging that the Licensed Technology, services, or deliverables infringe or misappropriate intellectual property rights.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity must contain the usual exclusion for infringement caused by Customer modifications.
elements.evidence: No Customer-modification exclusion appears in Article XIII-A.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity must contain the usual exclusion for infringement caused by combinations with items not supplied or approved by Vendor.
elements.evidence: No combination exclusion appears in Article XIII-A.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity must contain the usual exclusion for infringement caused by compliance with Customer specifications.
elements.evidence: No Customer-specification exclusion appears in Article XIII-A.

elements.element: Vendor must have an infringement remedy to procure Customer’s continued right to use the affected item.
elements.evidence: The redlined clause contains no procure-right remedy.

elements.element: Vendor must have an infringement remedy to modify the affected item so it becomes non-infringing.
elements.evidence: The redlined clause contains no modification remedy.

elements.element: Vendor must have an infringement remedy to replace the affected item with a non-infringing alternative.
elements.evidence: The redlined clause contains no replacement remedy.

elements.element: Vendor must provide a refund remedy if the infringement cannot otherwise be resolved.
elements.evidence: The redlined clause contains no infringement-related refund remedy.

elements.element: Vendor’s indemnity liability must be subject to a super-cap equal to three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: Article XIII-A states that the indemnity is not subject to Article XIII’s liability limitations and supplies no separate three-times-annual-fees cap.

result.reason: The Vendor indemnity substantially implements the preferred Vendor-side protection and procedures, but the Customer breach-of-law trigger is malformed and potentially broader than intended. The retained statement making Licensee solely responsible for liability arising from exercise of the license rights also conflicts with the new Vendor IP-risk allocation. The fallback exclusions, infringement remedies, and 3× annual-fees super-cap are absent. The blanket carveout from all liability limitations also goes beyond what was necessary to state the requested indemnity.
